meta.title: Job costing with normal costing
meta.summary: Job costing versus process costing, the seven-step approach, actual and normal costing, budgeted overhead rates, source documents and the job cost record, and job costing in service firms.

videos.title: Job costing or process costing?
videos.take: Job costing tracks costs for distinct units; process costing averages costs over identical units

scenes.say: A custom trailer and a gallon of milk need different costing systems. Here's why.

scenes.heading: Two costing systems
scenes.say: Job costing is for distinct, custom products, like Prairie Gate's trailers, an audit or a car repair. Costs are collected for each job. Process costing is for masses of identical units, like milk or cereal, where cost is averaged over all units.

sub: Every trailer is built to order
scenes.say: Prairie Gate builds every trailer to a customer's specification, so it uses job costing. Each trailer is a job with its own number.

sub: Thousands of identical gallons
scenes.say: Later we'll meet Redwood Valley Creamery, which turns milk into identical gallons, so it uses process costing. That's Lecture 8.

sub: Custom options on a standard base
scenes.say: In practice many firms blend the two. A company that builds standard trailers with custom options might process-cost the base and job-cost the options.

scenes.q: Which business should use job costing?
scenes.say: Quick check. Which business should use job costing? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C. Each house is distinct. The others make identical units.

videos.title: Seven steps to cost a job
videos.take: Trace direct costs, then allocate indirect costs with a rate based on a cost-allocation base

scenes.say: Costing a job follows seven steps. Learn them once and they work for trailers, audits and repairs.

scenes.heading: Seven steps
scenes.say: One, identify the job. Two, trace its direct costs. Three, choose the base for allocating indirect costs. Four, identify the indirect cost pools. Five, compute the rate per unit of the base. Six, allocate indirect costs to the job. Seven, add it all up.

sub: A measure that links indirect
costs to jobs: labor hours, machine hours
scenes.say: The cost-allocation base links indirect costs to jobs. Prairie Gate's factory is labor-intensive, so it uses direct labor hours: jobs that take more hours use more supervision, power and equipment.

sub: Indirect cost pool ÷
quantity of the allocation base
scenes.say: The indirect cost rate is the indirect cost pool divided by the total quantity of the allocation base.

sub: Simple systems: one plant-wide rate
Refined systems: a rate per department or activity
scenes.say: A simple system uses one plant-wide pool and rate. More refined systems use a pool for each department or activity, which you'll see in Lectures 6 and 7.

scenes.q: Which step comes right after choosing the cost-allocation base and identifying the cost pool?
scenes.say: Quick check. After choosing the base and identifying the pool, what's next? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B: compute the rate, pool divided by base.

videos.title: Normal costing and budgeted rates
videos.take: Normal costing applies overhead with a budgeted annual rate so job costs are known as work is done

scenes.say: Actual overhead isn't known until year-end. But Karen needs job costs now. The answer is normal costing.

scenes.heading: Actual vs normal costing
scenes.say: Both systems trace actual direct costs. Actual costing allocates indirect costs at the actual rate, known only after the year ends. Normal costing uses a budgeted rate set at the start of the year, times the actual quantity of the base.

scenes.heading: Prairie Gate's 2027 budgeted rate
scenes.say: Prairie Gate budgets $1,728,000 of manufacturing overhead for 2027 and forty-eight thousand direct labor hours. Its budgeted overhead rate is thirty-six dollars per direct labor hour.

scenes.heading: Why an annual rate?
items: Overhead is seasonal: heating in winter
Costs aren't known until bills arrive
A monthly rate would make identical jobs cost differently
scenes.say: Why annual? Overhead is seasonal, with heating bills in winter. Volume swings month to month. Some bills arrive late. And a monthly rate would make an identical trailer cost more in January than in June.

sub: Differences are dealt with at year-end:
Lecture 5
scenes.say: Of course, budgets are rarely exact. The difference between overhead applied and overhead actually incurred is handled at year-end, in Lecture 5.

scenes.q: Budgeted overhead $900,000; budgeted machine hours 30,000. A job uses 12 machine hours. Overhead applied?
scenes.say: Quick check. Budgeted overhead nine hundred thousand; budgeted machine hours thirty thousand. A job uses twelve machine hours. How much overhead is applied? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. The rate is $30 an hour, times twelve: $360.

videos.title: Source documents
videos.take: Materials requisitions and labor time records feed each job cost record

scenes.say: Where do the numbers on a job come from? Three documents, usually digital now.

scenes.heading: Three source documents
scenes.say: The job cost record collects every cost of one job. A materials requisition records materials issued to a specific job. A labor time record shows the hours each worker spent on each job.

scenes.heading: Requisition #2291 · Job 418
scenes.say: Requisition twenty-two ninety-one issues forty lengths of steel tubing, two axles and four wheels to job four-eighteen: $5,400. A second requisition adds the flooring and lights later.

sub: Barcode scans and time apps
post costs to jobs in real time
scenes.say: Today these are mostly digital. Workers scan a job barcode at each station, and materials are scanned out of the storeroom, so job costs update in real time.

sub: Sum of all open job cost records
scenes.say: Add up the job cost records for every unfinished job and you get the balance of the work-in-process control account.

scenes.q: Which document shows how many hours a welder spent on job 418?
scenes.say: Quick check. Which document shows a welder's hours on job four-eighteen? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B, the labor time record.

videos.title: Costing trailer #418
videos.take: Job cost = direct materials + direct labor + overhead applied at the budgeted rate

scenes.say: Let's put the seven steps together and cost trailer four-eighteen, a twenty-four-foot livestock trailer.

scenes.heading: Job cost record · Trailer #418
scenes.say: Trailer four-eighteen used $6,200 of direct materials. Workers logged eighty hours at thirty dollars, $2,400. Overhead is applied at the budgeted rate of thirty-six dollars for each of those eighty hours, $2,880. Total job cost: $11,480.

scenes.heading: Was it profitable?
scenes.say: The customer paid $14,500, so the job's gross margin is $3,020, or about twenty-one percent.

sub: Similar trailers: ~80 hours
Bid cost + markup for value chain costs
scenes.say: Karen uses job records like this to bid on future work. A similar trailer will take about eighty hours, and her price must also cover design, delivery and administration, which aren't in the job cost.

sub: Compare actual hours and materials
with the bid on every job
scenes.say: After each job, comparing actual hours and materials with the bid shows whether the estimates, or the welders, need attention.

scenes.q: Job 419: DM $4,800, 60 labor hours at $30, overhead $36 an hour. Total cost?
scenes.say: Quick check. Job four-nineteen: direct materials forty-eight hundred, sixty labor hours at thirty dollars, overhead thirty-six an hour. Total cost? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Job costing in services
videos.take: Service firms cost each engagement with direct professional labor plus allocated support costs

scenes.say: Job costing isn't just for factories. Accounting firms, hospitals and repair shops cost every job too.

scenes.heading: Same steps, different words
scenes.say: In an accounting firm, the job is an engagement, the main direct cost is professional labor, and indirect costs are rent, administrative staff and technology.

scenes.heading: Lyon & Co. CPAs: audit of Prairie Gate
scenes.say: Lyon and Company, a Marshall accounting firm, estimates four hundred professional hours at sixty dollars for Prairie Gate's audit: $24,000. Support costs are allocated at one hundred ten percent of professional labor, $26,400. The engagement will cost $50,400, and a twenty-five percent markup gives a bid of $63,000.

sub: Service job costs go to expense,
not finished goods
scenes.say: With no inventory, a service firm's job costs go straight to expense. But job costing still drives pricing, staffing and profitability analysis.

sub: Overruns signal scope creep
or a bid that was too low
scenes.say: Firms track budgeted versus actual hours on every engagement. Overruns signal scope creep or a bid that was too low.

scenes.q: An engagement uses 150 hours at $70, with support at 90% of labor. Total cost?
scenes.say: Quick check. An engagement uses a hundred fifty hours at seventy dollars, with support at ninety percent of labor. Total cost? Pause and pick.

warmup: Your car repair invoice lists parts, labor hours and 'shop supplies'. Which are direct and which are allocated?
Parts and labor are traced; shop supplies is an allocated overhead charge. Same structure as a job cost record.

Value-chain costs outside manufacturing (design, delivery, admin) average 12% of manufacturing cost. A competitor is rumored to bid $11,500 each.

Manufacturing: 5,200 + 2,100 + 2,520 = 9,820. Full: 9,820 × 1.12 = 10,998; bid ≈ $12,098. Matching $11,500 still covers full cost (margin ~4.6%); consider spare capacity, which costs are truly incremental, and future county work. Fewer hours lower DL and applied overhead: 55 hours → 5,200 + 1,650 + 1,980 = 8,830.
exam: Distinguish actual costing from normal costing and explain why most firms use normal costing.
Both trace actual direct costs; actual applies actual indirect rates (known at year-end), normal applies budgeted annual rates to actual quantities. Normal gives timely, stable job costs.
